1: ---
2: name: rigorous-proof
3: description: Use Yui to make an existing mathematical proof self-contained as structured NL0 with Audit A, then optionally translate it through typed interfaces into Lean with source-faithful Audit B. Supports NL0-only, translation from an accepted NL0, and full workflows. Do not infer proof correctness from schema checks or introduce unproved assumptions to close a goal.
4: ---
5: 
6: # Yui: rigorous proof development
7: 
8: Use the smallest requested track. Preserve the original problem, hypotheses,
9: definitions and proof route. The two stages share one specification and explicit
10: invalidation rules; completing stage one does not require stage two.
11: 
12: The installed skill root is the directory containing this `SKILL.md`. Keep
13: `config.json`, `nl0/`, `nl02lean/` and `toolchain/` beside it; no enclosing
14: `rigorous-proof/` subdirectory or particular checkout name is required.
15: 
16: ## Select a stage
17: 
18: Before dispatch, follow [target selection](nl0/references/target-selection.md).
19: Resolve a clear intended theorem yourself without asking again; ask the user
20: only when the intended target remains ambiguous. Freeze the complete selected
21: statement(s), including standing assumptions, as an explicit job input.
22: 
23: The invoking agent owns request/configuration collection and dispatch. Follow
24: [installed operation](nl0/references/operation.md) to identify explicit proof inputs,
25: ask once for missing active-phase model/reasoning/speed settings and, for a
26: NL0, full or translation request, an explicit per-case worker count N, then call
27: `nl0/scripts/yui.py run` (or prepare/execute). Retain settings already supplied by
28: the user; do not call a separate intent-classification model. Do not silently
29: choose a worker count from defaults or `auto`; obtain a positive integer or
30: the user's explicit confirmation of a proposed number. N bounds local R-node
31: reviews and, in a separate phase, local Lean proofs. NL0/Audit A and
32: Lean preparation/proofs/assembly/Audit B have separate phase profiles. The user
33: does not prepare queues, task packets or controller jobs manually.
34: The invoking owner follows [foreground handoff and monitoring](nl0/references/owner-observation.md):
35: normally dispatch with `--detach`, verify the owned processes, and register one
36: host heartbeat for a bounded check every ten minutes. Record the actual schedule
37: ID, report that mathematical work is still pending, then end the current
38: foreground turn. Never keep the owner active through sleep/poll loops. Each
39: scheduled check ends its turn as well. `DISPATCHED` is not workflow completion.
40: If host scheduling is unavailable, disclose that and return manual status/cancel
41: commands; do not claim that a monitor was registered. Frozen author/proof/reviewer
42: stages perform only their assigned roles and never schedule owner monitoring or
43: redispatch the workflow.
44: 
45: For missing external originals, follow [ordered source retrieval](nl0/references/source-retrieval.md):
46: arXiv, Google full-text search, Google DOI discovery, then confirmed-DOI Sci-Hub
47: lookup with ordinary browser readback when needed. Reuse an already available
48: adequate primary source; retrieval alone does not establish theorem fidelity.
49: At invocation disclose the [conditional-source policy](nl0/references/conditional-sources.md):
50: inaccessible primary texts can permit continued work from complete explicit
51: secondary statements, but the final result remains conditional. Show each
52: actual warning and include warn.json/warn.md in the final report. Never label
53: unverified sources or a qualified workflow as an ordinary full PASS.
54: 
55: Default permanent output is `<problem-directory>/rigorous-proof/<run-id>/`,
56: outside the installed skill. Multiple problems own separate outputs, contexts,
57: queues and ledgers. Use normal local repair unless a first-pass measurement is
58: explicitly requested. Runtime and software controls are fully inside this skill;
59: no repository example/support directory or old test result is required.
60: Positively identified temporary remote-service failures retry within the same
61: isolated thread, preserving its drafts and tool receipts. Keep the selected
62: profile and record every fault/wait; use [operational recovery](nl0/references/operation.md#remote-service-recovery)
63: for backoff, cancellation and explicit continuation of an already exited run.
64: 
65: 1. **NL0 and Audit A.** Use [Audit A's shared acceptance requirements](nl0/references/audit-a.md#shared-mathematical-acceptance-requirements)
66:    as the single mathematical standard for both author and auditor.
67:    Read [the NL0 stage](nl0/references/nl0-stage.md),
68:    [format](nl0/references/nl0-format.md), [self-containment](nl0/references/self-containment.md),
69:    [authoring](nl0/references/nl0-authoring.md), and Audit A's role-specific execution protocol.
70:    Read [external-source review](nl0/references/external-theorems.md) for citations
71:    and [logical packaging](nl0/references/logical-rules.md) for local assumptions.
72:    Use `nl0/scripts/nl0.py`; its explicit accounting is not a mathematical prover.
73:    Controllers and reviewers follow [completion and local repair](nl0/references/review-execution.md)
74:    for global-first parallel R coverage, exact evidence inheritance and stage boundaries.
75: 2. **Translate an accepted NL0 and run Audit B.** Verify the supplied Audit A
76:    authority and exact source version first; do not reconstruct or re-audit an
77:    unchanged proof. Start with [minimal translation](nl02lean/references/minimal-translation.md).
78:    Read [translation](nl02lean/references/stage.md),
79:    [the working sequence](nl02lean/references/integrated-workflow.md), and
80:    [Audit B](nl02lean/references/audit-b.md). Operators use
81:    [execution and file-based control](nl02lean/references/execution-protocol.md)
82:    for parallel queues, status and stops; workers need only their frozen packet.
83:    After local proofs complete, the serial postprocessing author follows
84:    [assembly and source-facing export](nl02lean/references/assembly.md),
85:    then hands actual checked evidence to a separate independent Audit B reviewer.
86:    Use
87:    `nl02lean/scripts/source_preparation.py` for bounded shared extraction,
88:    then `workflow.py` for source/IR freeze, proof work and final gates.
89: 3. **Full workflow.** Complete track one, then track two. A changed mathematical
90:    statement or new theorem returns to the affected NL0/Audit A boundary.
91: 
92: ## Mathematical invariants
93: 
94: - Accepted NL0 is a complete natural-language proof relative to explicit H/E/M,
95:   fixed logic and its hash-bound verified background supplement. Important
96:   tools remain explicit; ordinary correct elementary reasoning needs no
97:   exhaustive calculation chain. See [background notes](nl0/references/background-notes.md).
98: - Within NL0, each inference uses only its direct inputs, global definitions and explicitly
99:   established in-scope local facts or positively checked node-local background
100:   notes. Notes never add H or repair a substantive gap. Source papers and producer proof bodies do
101:   not fill gaps in a task packet.
102: - Preserve one global mathematical identity while allowing local Lean views.
103:   Actual cross-view conversions need checked proofs. In stage two, the pinned
104:   Mathlib environment is freely available without NL0 M registration.
105: - Shared mathematical extraction is a bounded local change at translation entry.
106:   Review its new producer and substitution cuts; inherit unchanged evidence.
107:   Freeze the revised NL0 before final IR and worker packets.
108: - Local conditional bodies may run concurrently. Assembly must discharge every
109:   internal dependency with an actual checked proof; conditional checks alone
110:   are not a final result.
111: - Audit B checks every external E and the complete target P, including its
112:   hypotheses, against actual Lean types and relevant definitions. Supply short
113:   direct/equivalent correspondence explanations; an independent reviewer verifies
114:   them. Check fresh Lean closure and trust, without a Mathlib-to-NL0 use ledger.
115:   Neither author notes nor a compiler pass are semantic approval.
116: - Stop on a judged substantive mathematical gap. Ordinary expansion and local
117:   verifiable corrections remain allowed. Difficulty or elapsed time does not
118:   establish that a mathematical claim is false.
119: 
120: ## Clean execution and accounting
121: 
122: Operators use [execution terminology](nl0/references/terminology.md) to distinguish
123: Codex conversations, native subagents, Yui jobs, worker slots and controllers.
124: Use the logical phase names **NL0 worker**, **preprocessing worker**,
125: **formalization workers (N slots)** and **postprocessing worker**. A logical
126: worker may contain several separate author/reviewer threads and program steps;
127: N limits concurrent local R reviews and local Lean proof jobs in their separate phases.
128: Report executor termination separately from mathematical acceptance.
129: 
130: Read [isolation](nl0/references/isolation.md) and [measurement](nl0/references/measurement.md)
131: before any model test or benchmark. Run model authoring, planning, proof and
132: review stages through the isolated carrier. The interactive developer's memory,
133: other personal skills, expert packages, old task outputs and hidden reference
134: proofs are never an input source for these stages.
135: 
136: The Yui arm receives only the declared Yui rules and task material. The direct
137: arm receives a minimal task/tool contract and the same mathematical inputs,
138: without Yui planning, strategy or shared-proof guidance. Log actual transmitted
139: instructions, complete allowed inputs, tool schemas/results, model identity,
140: phase, usage and health. Never execute model-generated Python or shell text.
141: 
142: Collect the active phase profiles as described above. `config.json` supplies
143: defaults only when explicitly selected. The current isolated carrier supports
144: Standard speed and checks model/effort availability without fallback. Freeze
145: and record each stage's selected profile;
146: never silently substitute a stronger model or fallback.
147: Resolve the confirmed concurrency before dispatch and record its basis; do not
148: claim an unknown backend maximum. N limits local R-node reviews, then local
149: Lean proof jobs in a later phase. NL0 authoring, global Audit A, preparation,
150: interface work, assembly and Audit B use one serial lane per case.
151: Count root/controller, worker, review and retry calls. Cached/reasoning tokens
152: are subsets of input/output totals, not extra tokens. Missing usage is unknown.
153: 
154: Return the exact accepted scope, source/formal artifacts, unresolved citations
155: or gaps, actual execution health, time/token breakdown, and reproducible commands.
156: Do not claim a universal NL0 compiler, an unconditional proof of literature
157: inputs, completed Audit C, or acceleration from this prototype alone.

value.full_target:
Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
value.conclusion: dim_H(F)=D+1, where F=E×[0,1] has the Euclidean product metric and D=dim_H(E); equivalently dim_H(E×[0,1])=dim_H(E)+1 in ℝ^{n+1}.

record.type: extended nonnegative diameter of a subset of a metric or extended metric space
record.definition: For an extended metric space X and A⊆X, diam(A)=sup{edist(x,y):x∈A,y∈A} in [0,∞], with supremum of the empty set equal to 0. On a metric space edist is ordinary distance viewed in [0,∞]. This is the native Metric.ediam. When diam(A) is bounded by a finite scale we identify it with its finite nonnegative real value. In particular empty sets and singletons have diameter zero.

record.definition:
For a Euclidean set \(A\), exponent \(s>0\), and scale \(\delta>0\), put

\[
H^s_\delta(A)=\inf\left\{\sum_i(\operatorname{diam}U_i)^s:
 A\subseteq\bigcup_iU_i,\quad\operatorname{diam}U_i\leq\delta\right\},
\qquad H^s(A)=\sup_{\delta>0}H^s_\delta(A).
\]

Covers are countable, with empty members contributing zero.

record.type: native Hausdorff measures on Borel extended metric spaces, indexed by real exponents
record.definition: μH[d] on a Borel extended metric space X denotes MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure d, defined natively as Measure.mkMetric(r↦r^d), the metric outer-measure construction with diameter gauge r^d followed by its Borel measure. The metric outer construction is the supremum over positive extended scales r of the infimum of Σ_i (sup_{h:U_i≠∅} diam(U_i)^d) over sequences U:ℕ→Set X covering the set and satisfying diam(U_i)≤r. Empty summands are zero, including at exponent zero. Native ENNReal real powers are used. The value formula for the resulting measure on arbitrary subsets is established by the registered native theorem; its identification with H for positive exponents is proved below.

record.type: Hausdorff dimension of a subset of a metric space, valued in [0,∞]
record.definition: For a subset A of a metric space with its Borel structure, dim_H(A)=sup{u:u∈[0,∞) is finite and μH[u](A)=∞}, with supremum of the empty set zero. The metric space may be borelized when no measurable structure was specified. This is the native dimH definition. Thus dim_H(∅)=0 by this convention. In this task it is applied to Euclidean subsets and the Euclidean product metric of V(n)×ℝ.

record.definition: F=E×I={(x,t):x∈E,t∈I}, using the squared-distance product metric specified in V. Its Euclidean identification is the concatenation map to V(n+1).
D=dim_H(E). When finiteness is proved, finite dimensions are also viewed as nonnegative real numbers through the canonical inclusion ℝ≥0→[0,∞].

record.type: predicate on subsets of metric spaces
record.definition: Compact(A) means that every family of open sets whose union contains A has a finite subfamily whose union contains A. The word compact has this finite-open-subcover meaning throughout.

record.type: Lebesgue measure on the Borel real line, also evaluated as outer measure on arbitrary sets
record.definition: λ is the native MeasureTheory.volume on ℝ, equivalently the Lebesgue measure whose outer measure is the infimum of sums of lengths of countable open-interval covers. As for any measure, λ is monotone, has λ(∅)=0, and is countably additive on disjoint measurable sets. These measure axioms are part of the measure structure, not any assertion of measurability of the arbitrary covering sets in this proof.

1: # Hausdorff dimension of a product with an interval
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: Elias M. Stein and Rami Shakarchi, *Real Analysis: Measure Theory,
6: Integration, and Hilbert Spaces*, Princeton Lectures in Analysis III,
7: Chapter 7, Problems, exercise 9, printed page 388.
8: Book DOI: [10.1515/9781400835560](https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400835560).
9: 
10: > 9. Let \(E\) be a compact set in \(\mathbb R^{d-1}\). Show that
11: > \(\dim(E\times I)=\dim(E)+1\), where \(I\) is the unit interval in
12: > \(\mathbb R\).
13: 
14: ## Fixed interpretation and complete target
15: 
16: Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
17: 2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
18: \(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
19: the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.
20: 
21: Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
22: compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
23: with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove
24: 
25: \[
26: \dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
27: \]
28: 
29: The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
30: formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
31: 
32: ## Fixed natural-language proof
33: 
34: For a Euclidean set \(A\), exponent \(s>0\), and scale \(\delta>0\), put
35: 
36: \[
37: H^s_\delta(A)=\inf\left\{\sum_i(\operatorname{diam}U_i)^s:
38:  A\subseteq\bigcup_iU_i,\quad\operatorname{diam}U_i\leq\delta\right\},
39: \qquad H^s(A)=\sup_{\delta>0}H^s_\delta(A).
40: \]
41: 
42: Covers are countable, with empty members contributing zero. This
43: unnormalized Hausdorff measure gives the usual Hausdorff dimension. We use
44: its critical-exponent characterization: \(H^s(A)=0\) if
45: \(s>\dim_H A\), and \(H^s(A)=\infty\) if \(0<s<\dim_H A\).
46: Conversely, zero measure implies \(\dim_H A\leq s\), and infinite
47: measure implies \(\dim_H A\geq s\).
48: 
49: Write \(D=\dim_H E\) and \(F=E\times[0,1]\). First \(0\leq D\leq n\).
50: Indeed, compactness makes \(E\) bounded. When \(n>0\), a box containing
51: it admits a cover by at most \(Ch^{-n}\) cubes of side at most \(h\),
52: for \(0<h\leq1\). Here \(C\) depends only on that box. Each cube has
53: diameter at most \(\sqrt n h\). For any \(s>n\), the total \(s\)-cost
54: is at most \(C n^{s/2}h^{s-n}\to0\). These arbitrarily fine covers
55: give \(H^s(E)=0\) and hence \(D\leq n\). If \(n=0\), nonemptiness
56: makes \(E=\mathbb R^0\), a singleton of zero \(s\)-cost for every
57: \(s>0\); thus \(D=0\).
58: 
59: ### Upper bound
60: 
61: When \(n=0\), \(F\) is isometric to \([0,1]\). Dividing this interval
62: into \(N\) equal pieces gives total \(a\)-cost \(N^{1-a}\to0\) for
63: every \(a>1\), proving \(\dim_H F\leq1=D+1\).
64: For this upper-bound argument now assume \(n\geq1\).
65: 
66: Fix \(q>D\). Since \(q>0\) and \(H^q(E)=0\), for every
67: \(0<r\leq1\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) there is a countable cover
68: \((U_i)\) of \(E\) with nonempty-member diameters
69: \(0<r_i\leq r\) and \(\sum_i r_i^q<\varepsilon\).
70: The positive-diameter requirement costs nothing: start with a cover of
71: cost below \(\varepsilon/2\); replace each zero-diameter singleton by
72: a ball of diameter at most \(r\), choosing the \(i\)-th replacement
73: to have \(q\)-cost less than \(\varepsilon2^{-i-2}\). The added cost
74: is less than \(\varepsilon/2\). Discard empty members.
75: 
76: Let \(N_i=\lceil1/r_i\rceil\). Partition \([0,1]\) into \(N_i\)
77: closed intervals of length \(1/N_i\leq r_i\). Because \(r_i\leq1\),
78: \(N_i\leq2/r_i\). The corresponding products with \(U_i\) form a
79: countable cover of \(F\). Each has Euclidean diameter at most
80: \(\sqrt2 r_i\), and their total \((q+1)\)-cost is at most
81: 
82: \[
83: \sum_iN_i(\sqrt2 r_i)^{q+1}
84: \leq2(\sqrt2)^{q+1}\sum_i r_i^q
85: <2(\sqrt2)^{q+1}\varepsilon.
86: \]
87: 
88: For any target scale \(\delta>0\), choose
89: \(r\leq\min(1,\delta/\sqrt2)\), then let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
90: Thus \(H^{q+1}_\delta(F)=0\) for every scale, so
91: \(H^{q+1}(F)=0\) and \(\dim_H F\leq q+1\). Letting \(q\downarrow D\)
92: gives \(\dim_H F\leq D+1\).
93: 
94: ### Lower bound when \(D>0\)
95: 
96: Fix \(0<s<D\). Then \(H^s(E)=\infty\), so
97: \(H^s_\delta(E)\) becomes arbitrarily large as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
98: We claim that, for every \(\delta>0\),
99: 
100: \[
101: H^s_\delta(E)\leq H^{s+1}_\delta(F).                 \tag{1}
102: \]
103: 
104: Take an arbitrary countable \(\delta\)-cover \((V_i)_{i\geq0}\) of
105: \(F\), discarding empty members. Define
106: \(\rho_i=\operatorname{diam}V_i\),
107: \(A_i=\pi_{\mathbb R^n}(V_i)\), and
108: \(B_i=\pi_{\mathbb R}(V_i)\). Coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz,
109: so both projected diameters are at most \(\rho_i\leq\delta\).
110: For \(\varepsilon>0\), put
111: 
112: \[
113: \eta_i=\frac{\varepsilon2^{-i-1}}{1+\rho_i^s}>0.
114: \]
115: 
116: Enclose \(B_i\) in an open interval \(J_i\) of length at most
117: \(\rho_i+\eta_i\): its supremum minus infimum is at most \(\rho_i\),
118: and an enlargement of total width \(\eta_i\) suffices. This avoids
119: assuming that the arbitrary covering sets or their projections are measurable.
120: 
121: For each \(t\in[0,1]\), the sets \(A_i\) for which \(t\in J_i\)
122: cover \(E\). Indeed, a point \((x,t)\in F\) belongs to some \(V_i\),
123: giving \(x\in A_i\) and \(t\in B_i\subset J_i\). Their diameters
124: are at most \(\rho_i\). Consequently, with \(c=H^s_\delta(E)\),
125: 
126: \[
127: c\leq\sum_i\rho_i^s\mathbf1_{J_i}(t)\quad(t\in[0,1]).
128: \]
129: 
130: The constant \(c\) is finite: compactness gives a finite cover of \(E\)
131: by balls of diameter at most \(\delta\), with finite \(s\)-cost.
132: Each summand is nonnegative and measurable since \(J_i\) is open.
133: Integrate over \([0,1]\), of Lebesgue measure one, and use Tonelli's
134: theorem for this nonnegative series. Since
135: \(|J_i\cap[0,1]|\leq\rho_i+\eta_i\),
136: 
137: \[
138: \begin{aligned}
139: c&\leq\sum_i\rho_i^s|J_i\cap[0,1]|\\
140:  &\leq\sum_i\rho_i^{s+1}+\sum_i\eta_i\rho_i^s
141:  \leq\sum_i\rho_i^{s+1}+\varepsilon.
142: \end{aligned}
143: \]
144: 
145: If the first series is infinite the desired inequality is immediate;
146: otherwise let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\). Take the infimum over the
147: arbitrary covers to obtain (1). As its left side is unbounded at small
148: scales, \(H^{s+1}(F)=\infty\), giving \(\dim_H F\geq s+1\).
149: Letting \(s\uparrow D\) proves \(\dim_H F\geq D+1\).
150: 
151: ### Lower bound when \(D=0\)
152: 
153: Choose \(x_0\in E\). The map \(t\mapsto(x_0,t)\) is an isometric
154: embedding of \([0,1]\) into \(F\), so dimension monotonicity gives
155: \(\dim_H F\geq\dim_H[0,1]\). This interval has dimension one:
156: equal-length covers gave the upper bound above. For \(0<s<1\), any
157: \(\delta\)-cover with diameters \(\rho_i\leq\delta\) satisfies
158: \(\sum_i\rho_i\geq1\). To see this, enclose its nonempty members
159: in open intervals of lengths at most \(\rho_i+\varepsilon2^{-i-1}\),
160: use countable subadditivity of length to get
161: \(1\leq\sum_i\rho_i+\varepsilon\), and let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
162: Hence \(\sum_i\rho_i^s\geq\delta^{s-1}\sum_i\rho_i
163: \geq\delta^{s-1}\to\infty\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
164: This proves the lower bound one. Thus \(\dim_H F\geq1=D+1\),
165: including when \(n=0\).
166: 
167: Together the bounds establish the required equality.
168:

170:

172: tests. It is a natural-language input, not an NL0 artifact, an Audit A receipt,
173: a Lean proof, or a passing test result. Future runs must independently produce
174: and check those artifacts. The basic Hausdorff-measure and integration facts
175: used here must be registered by that future NL0/Audit A workflow.

246: unchecked sources. A missing complete statement remains a missing input; do not
247: invent it. Full acceptance requires actual primary-source verification.
248: 
249: ## A3. Structure
250:

249: ## A3. Structure
250: 
251: Run `nl0.py check`. Confirm that every retained node is on P's dependency
252: closure and every internal/target has one complete producer. Derive reachability
253: by AND closure: accept an R's output only after all its inputs are accepted and
254: the R itself passes mathematical review. Mere existence of a path is inadequate.
255: Only E/M/H are trusted source proposition kinds; a proof with no mathematical
256: inputs must still contain an actual permitted calculation/logical argument.
257: 
258: ## A4. Review every inference
259: 
260: Apply verified-background-1 while retaining every check below. An eligible
261: omitted basic fact receives a positively checked background note and does not
262: fail solely for missing input accounting. Ordinary correct elementary
263: compression needs no exhaustive displayed chain. Substantive missing grounds,
264: conditions, sources or proof still block. The accepted local material includes
265: the version-bound supplement; it cannot be reconstructed silently from memory.
266: 
267: First check three closures from the actual text:
268: 
269: - **statement_closure**: input/output statements include every claimed formula,
270:   condition, binder and semantic convention. No producer proof is needed to
271:   understand them. Source notation and inherited equation numbers are not content.
272: - **object_closure**: actual object occurrences map to legitimate declarations
273:   in scope. Compare text to the inventory, not the inventory to itself. Check
274:   input instantiation, witness existence and parameter dependence.
275: - **dependency_closure**: actual factual uses map to direct inputs, prior
276:   in-scope local proofs or fixed logical/calculation steps. An ancestor not
277:   listed as input is unavailable; prior/source proof bodies supply no extra fact.
278: 
279: Then check the six mathematical obligations below. Every check needs a separate
280: `{verdict, notes, evidence, locations}` record with precise packet locations and
281: an explanation. Repeating author notes or generic assurances is not review.
282: 
283: 1. **inputs**: the cited propositions are the actual graph inputs and true
284:    earlier results, original H, or verified sources. They are instantiated
285:    with compatible parameters and definitions.
286: 2. **argument**: every step is justified and sufficient. Explicitly inspect
287:    domain, limits, operator applications, integrability, sign, constants,
288:    uniformity, degeneracies, and selected witnesses where material.
289: 3. **dependency_accounting**: each declared input has an identifiable role;
290:    no additional nontrivial theorem is hidden in “clearly,” an analogy,
291:    a definition, or a convenient abstract interface. Locally derived facts are
292:    permitted only after their derivation. This is accounting for the present
293:    argument, not a claim that its input set is minimal across all proofs.
294:    A named theorem is also an imported fact unless its full required result
295:    is actually proved locally. Explaining why its hypotheses hold is an
296:    application check, not a proof of that theorem. For example, “apply FTC,”
297:    “Fubini applies because the function is integrable,” “compactness gives
298:    uniform continuity,” and “a dominated limit may be integrated” require
299:    declared E/M inputs or complete earlier local proofs of the needed results.
300:    Familiarity, a descriptive theorem name, or inclusion in an author-written
301:    calculation-policy sentence cannot waive this obligation. Ordinary valid textbook compression is allowed for eligible background;
302:    substantive tools and missing arguments still need their actual grounds.
303:    An abstract finite-dimensional, tensor or localization lemma is not
304:    automatically a finite arithmetic identity: inspect its displayed map,
305:    inverse, basis or other derivation, or require the actual declared source.
306: 4. **output**: the derived theorem is exactly the output's full statement,
307:    including quantifier order, assumptions, scope, constants and endpoints.
308: 5. **scope**: temporary assumptions are correctly closed into the implication,
309:    negation, cases, or other allowed rule. Check binder freshness and witness
310:    escape. Introduce/discharge metadata alone is not proof. Do not reclassify
311:    a temporary assumption as an original H.
312: 6. **applicability**: check every E/M obligation using its actual bindings and
313:    input/local proofs, including any proved bridge. For each E application A
314:    record separate binding, per-hypothesis and conclusion reviews and the N
315:    bridge IDs. “The theorem applies” is not a hypothesis mapping.
316: 
317: Finally complete **packet_replay**, the tenth check. A fresh context reviews
318: the exact packet, Yui rules and logged pinned-mathlib queries for verified
319: background, without original-source proofs, other R
320: bodies, old NL0, author audit notes or prefilled verdicts. Record actual carrier,
321: packet hash, prior exposure, mathematical materials read and execution evidence.
322: Source fidelity is a separate check. Same-context rereading is a diagnostic,
323: not fresh replay. This standard does not authorize new agent/service dispatch;
324: keep an unperformed replay UNVERIFIED. Metadata cannot authenticate a claimed
325: identity or isolation; preserve actual execution evidence and disclose limits.
326: 
327: For an authorized clean packet replay, expose only that frozen packet as a
328: task document, plus the Yui procedure. The clean packet carrier exposes controlled read-only pinned-mathlib
329: queries and source probes for background notes, never arbitrary local files.
330: Source/signature verification is a separate stage with its own disclosed inputs.
331: 
332: Use `audit-template` for scaffolds. Every generated verdict starts UNVERIFIED.
333: Serialization may preserve actually made judgments, but cannot infer PASS from
334: author notes, populated fields, successful hashes or absence of exceptions.
335: Ineligible missing content blocks acceptance. Eligible routine background
336: may be positively checked and recorded, never silently assumed from memory. Return the defect to authoring and review the newly frozen version.
337: 
338: Stop granting acceptance at the first unsupported implication. Other diagnostic
339: checks may continue, but a blocked descendant cannot receive a whole-proof
340: pass. Report exact premises -> conclusion and the affected closure. Repairs
341: require a new graph hash and replacement audit, never a silently stronger H.
342: 
343: An ordinary omission or verifiable local mistake may return to routine NL0
344: completion without interrupting the user for each correction. Review the
345: revised argument before accepting it. If completion stalls, apply
346: [routine completion and substantive proof gaps](nl0-authoring.md#routine-completion-and-substantive-proof-gaps)
347: to assess whether construction must stop; do not turn every omitted detail
348: into a substantive-gap report or silently begin a new proof strategy.
349: 
350: ## A5. Adversarial target checks
351: 
352: Check actual excluded/included endpoints, zero/degenerate objects, a.e. versus
353: everywhere, scalar/representation changes, and constant uniformity. Negative
354: controls must distinguish machine-detectable corruption (unknown IDs, changed
355: evidence) from semantic corruption (wrong argument with unchanged structure).
356: A failed counterexample search or a valid JSON file cannot establish correctness.
357: 
358: ## Acceptance and report
359: 
360: Behavioral controls must include an opaque formula output, a source-only object,
361: an unlisted theorem and an unsupported witness. A real reviewer receives neutral
362: packets without labels, old reviews or expected answers; the owner's answer key
363: stays outside its input directory. Require located findings, not just verdicts.
364: Manually assigning FAIL only tests receipt handling, not model detection. If no
365: reviewer ran, report NOT_RUN. `prepare-review-cases.py --help` prepares a small
366: control set without calling a model or claiming an isolation experiment.
367: 
368: Grant `DRAFT-AUDIT-PASSED` only if A0–A5 are actually completed for the exact
369: frozen artifact, every required review is PASS, source evidence is verified,
370: and P closes without extra assumptions. Say “same-context self-audit” when
371: that is the execution mode. `nl0.py --audit` verifies the hash-bound review
372: record's completeness, not the truth of the reviewer statements. Preserve any
373: FAIL/UNVERIFIED report and identify the first gap; do not erase it after repair.
374: For access-limited sources, retain an explicit pending-citation list and
375: UNVERIFIED source judgments. A complete otherwise-passing review may authorize
376: only the [conditional continuation](conditional-sources.md); it is not an
377: unqualified whole-proof pass.

1: # Self-containment details
2: 
3: This is the detailed meaning of Audit A's `statement_closure`,
4: `object_closure` and `dependency_closure` requirements. The
5: [shared Audit A section](audit-a.md#shared-mathematical-acceptance-requirements)
6: is the acceptance authority for author and auditor; this annex supplies
7: interpretation and examples, not an independent permission policy.
8: 
9: ## Two boundaries
10: 
11: Accepted NL0 is a complete proof relative to its declared H/E/M roots, frozen
12: logical foundation and version-bound verified background notes. It is not an outline requiring the original manuscript to
13: recover missing definitions, formulas, assumptions, or arguments. E/M statements
14: are fully restated; their primary sources are inspected for provenance, not
15: used to supply unstated premises. The fixed library's own proof dependencies
16: need not be recopied. The target work's internal results must be proved here.
17: 
18: Every R must also be checkable from its packet alone: the complete statements
19: of its direct inputs, their required definitions/declarations, its complete
20: output, its local declarations, and its own argument. Another R's proof body,
21: an ancestor not listed as an input, an ambient original H, an original-source
22: crosswalk, or remembered material is not an additional mathematical resource.
23: Whole-target/source-fidelity checks are separate from this local proof check.
24: Under verified-background-1, local review may additionally verify routine
25: pinned-mathlib facts using logged read-only queries and record them in the
26: receipt. They join this R's effective dependencies, without new H or a graph
27: rewrite. See [background notes](background-notes.md). Mathematical uncertainty
28: still blocks; ordinary correct elementary compression alone does not.
29: 
30: Original theorem conditions are H nodes, including conditions that could be
31: encoded in a refined type. Parameters introduce ambient data/structures, not
32: an ambient stock of original hypotheses. For example, declare a vector and
33: put its required nonzero condition in H; do not write “nonzero vector” in its
34: parameter type and use that condition from an empty input list. The same rule
35: applies to characteristic/range conditions and equations. An R must list every
36: original H it actually uses. Standard structure operations/axioms and the fixed
37: finite-language rules remain available; no new substantive theorem is added.
38: 
39: An output must be understandable and callable without reading its producer's
40: argument. Include the actual equalities/inequalities, binder types, hypotheses,
41: parameter windows, constant dependencies, representatives and a.e./pointwise
42: meaning. Global defined notation can be expanded from the packet. A formula
43: number, theorem name, or paragraph location cannot replace mathematical content.
44: Source locators belong in provenance fields. New mathematical prose uses direct
45: input IDs and previously proved local F IDs, not inherited numbered references.
46: 
47: ## Object closure
48: 
49: For every mathematical object actually appearing in a statement, definition,
50: local declaration, or proof, locate one legitimate declaration:
51: 
52: 1. A frozen parameter, explicit logical primitive, or global D definition.
53:    State its meaning, type/domain and parameter dependence. Global primitives
54:    cover only core typed syntax, not a dictionary of subject-specific objects.
55:    New subjects use the same parameter/definition/local declaration mechanism;
56:    symbol registration never licenses a theorem.
57: 2. A binder inside the current proposition's full statement. Its scope remains
58:    that statement. A variable bound in an input does not become a free object
59:    in the consuming proof; instantiate the statement explicitly.
60: 3. A local declaration before first use, recording its kind, type, exact
61:    declaration, introduction basis, and scope. An arbitrary variable requires
62:    legitimate quantifier introduction; a definition uses already available
63:    objects; a witness requires an input or an earlier local existence proof.
64: 
65: A declaration cannot grant existence, uniqueness, invertibility, regularity,
66: or a desired property merely by naming an object. Those obligations require
67: proof. Any D guard needed to use the object must be a direct R input, not a
68: theorem silently recovered from ancestor closure. Record mutually compatible
69: choices and witness dependence. Temporary assumptions stay inside R and must
70: be correctly discharged. Branch witnesses, local facts and local notation
71: cannot escape their scopes. Export a quantified or conditional statement when
72: needed, rather than a free private name. Global names are reserved; dummy
73: variables may be reused in disjoint local scopes.
74: 
75: ## Dependency closure
76: 
77: Inventory actual factual uses from the prose back to their grounds, not just
78: from an input list forward to a generic `uses` list. Each substantive imported theorem, prior project lemma or original
79: assumption must be a direct input. Eligible omitted basic library uses are
80: recorded as verified audit notes in the effective dependency ledger. A definition supplies meaning, not a theorem. An R output is not its
81: own premise. Adding the desired formula as an unproved input is not a repair.
82: 
83: Explicit local calculations and fully proved intermediate facts may remain
84: inside R. Give a reused local fact a full F statement and identify its earlier
85: derivation and open assumptions. No separate graph vertex is needed for every
86: algebraic equality. A nontrivial imported result cannot be called a local
87: calculation. Substantive reusable lemmas should become N/R pairs; any fact
88: reused by another R must be exported in a complete proposition statement.
89: 
90: The controller owns `spec.logic.calculations` and the small core syntax table
91: (`nl0/scripts/foundations.py`). The clean author tool binds omitted metadata and
92: rejects extra author permissions or task-specific primitives. This fixed
93: language grants no MVT, FTC, Fubini, convergence, compactness or regularity
94: theorem. Such facts need a declared input or an actual local derivation.
95: An author-written permission claim, in any field or prose, has no authority.
96: Ordinary typed arithmetic notation is part of this fixed language: natural
97: numbers, integers, rationals, reals and complex numbers mean their standard
98: structures with usual numerals and operations. Finite calculations include
99: their zero/one laws, such as `a+0=a`, as well as explicit algebra/order
100: derivations. Do not demand a separate E/M for an operation token or an allowed
101: finite calculation. This does not grant calculus, topology or measure theorems.
102: Conversely, inspect an actual displayed local derivation before demanding a
103: duplicate E/M input for its conclusion. A named consequence proved by permitted
104: finite algebra/order steps is not an imported premise. If a local derivation
105: fails, locate its unsupported implication rather than its absent theorem name.
106: 
107: Metadata accounts for the argument but never replaces it. Copying all inputs
108: into a single `uses` record, registering a symbol without declaring it in the
109: proof, or writing a PASS label cannot establish closure.
110: 
111: ## Operational acceptance
112: 
113: 1. Author using the node template. Reverse-check the actual prose for missing
114:    declarations, unexpanded references and unlisted facts before freezing.
115: 2. Generate a packet for each R. The v2 generator supplies no original proof,
116:    producer proofs, provenance file locators, extra ancestor statements or
117:    undeclared ambient H. Direct source contracts and required definitions are
118:    included. Packet hashes bind the mathematical input actually reviewed.
119: 3. Review all closure/inference checks, admitting positively checked routine
120:    background notes under the shared policy. Record concrete packet locations and reasons for every verdict.
121: 4. Perform a fresh local replay with disclosed controlled background lookup. The reviewer gets the skill instructions
122:    and that packet plus logged pinned-mathlib queries, without original proof,
123:    other R bodies, author review
124:    notes, old verdicts, or an answer key. Record the actual carrier, packet hash,
125:    prior exposure and mathematical material read. Skill instructions supply no
126:    extra mathematical premise. Do not falsely claim a same-context rereading
127:    is a fresh replay. This rule does not authorize starting a new external
128:    service or agent; if the required carrier has not been used, keep replay
129:    UNVERIFIED and report that limit.
130:    Prior exposure means known task/proof material supplied or read in earlier
131:    contexts; this is not a claim about unknown pretraining contents. Learned
132:    mathematical knowledge cannot replace a missing declared premise or proof.
133: 5. An ineligible missing declaration, missing statement content, unlisted substantive theorem or need
134:    to look outside the packet blocks acceptance. Record the defect; do not
135:    silently repair it while assigning PASS. Return substantive/structural defects to authoring and review the frozen
136:    revision; eligible background notes need no author rewrite. Routine completion does not require a
137:    separate user interruption for every omission. Distinguish a representation
138:    defect from a substantive mathematical gap under the existing gap policy.
139: 
140: The code rejects explicit malformed references, inventories, scopes, guards
141: and receipts. It does not infer hidden hypotheses from property words in types,
142: or decide theorem applications by matching a list of mathematical names.
143: These semantic obligations apply equally to every subject and remain part of
144: author inspection and Audit A. An omitted inventory entry or unnamed
145: theorem hidden in prose still requires actual semantic review. Freshness and
146: truthful reviewer identity need execution evidence; record shape/hashes cannot
147: authenticate them. No natural-language audit is a Lean kernel certificate.

1: # External-theorem review: required Audit A standard
2: 
3: Apply this standard to every retained E and every actual use of E in an R.
4: An E keeps the full source theorem; a derived specialization or substantive
5: translation is an internal N. Use the data contract's audit version 2. These
6: are reviewer obligations: a filled record or matching hash cannot establish
7: that a publication or a mathematical assertion is genuine.
8: 
9: ## 1. Document identity
10: 
11: Obtain and read the actual primary document. Match author, title, source kind,
12: publication/release information and exact edition/version to its provenance.
13: Record a traceable original source, retrieval date, local document and hash.
14: A search snippet, model answer, secondary citation, or functioning DOI/URL
15: alone does not establish identity. Books, papers and reliable preprints can
16: qualify; a DOI and journal publication are not universal requirements. Record
17: the source category and grounds for treating it as an admissible source.
18: 
19: For missing originals, follow [ordered source retrieval](source-retrieval.md):
20: arXiv, Google full text, Google DOI discovery and confirmed-DOI Sci-Hub lookup.
21: Use normal browser readback when needed; unresolved access and verification
22: failures remain recorded. Then use the [conditional-source
23: procedure](conditional-sources.md) for unavailable text. Unavailable checks remain UNVERIFIED. A complete explicit
24: secondary statement can support a disclosed conditional run, not an ordinary
25: source-verification PASS.
26: 
27: ## 2. Occurrence of the result
28: 
29: Locate the claimed result in that document and version. Record theorem,
30: lemma, proposition or corollary label and page/section/paragraph/equation as
31: available; unnumbered results require an equally reproducible locator. Retain
32: the relevant primary text or a precise readback record bound to the document.
33: If the cited document merely points elsewhere without actually stating the
34: claimed result, follow and correct the source. An explicitly stated theorem in
35: an authoritative exposition can be cited as such; record its proof attribution
36: without claiming to have audited the referenced proof recursively.
37: Distinguish proved assertions from conjectures, questions, heuristics and
38: numerical observations. Preserve every condition of a conditional result.
39: 
40: ## 3. Statement fidelity
41: 
42: Compare the original full statement with the E statement, explicitly covering
43: objects, domains, scalar fields, spaces, hypotheses, regularity, quantifier
44: order, parameter intervals/endpoints, degeneracies, constant dependencies and
45: the exact conclusion (including a.e./everywhere, topology, uniformity,
46: existence/uniqueness and local/global scope). Record the notation map.
47: Faithful mathematical meaning, not word-for-word copying, is required.
48: Alpha-renaming is allowed. Never turn forall-x-exists-C_x into exists-C-forall-x.
49: 
50: ## 4. Complete context and definitions
51: 
52: Read the surrounding standing assumptions, definitions and conventions that
53: govern the result, including referenced context needed to understand it.
54: Capture any omitted chapter-wide hypotheses and normalization of measures,
55: norms, transforms, signs or scales. Map the source objects to the global D
56: ledger. Do not hide a condition outside the proof graph. A substantive
57: conversion requires an N proof; a renamed symbol is not that proof.
58: 
59: ## 5. Version status and source eligibility
60: 
61: Match every locator and statement to the chosen version. Check available
62: primary version histories, corrections, errata or withdrawal information at
63: the recorded date and scope. Record relevant findings and their effect;
64: explain use of an older version. Absence of a discovered correction is not
65: a guarantee that none exists. Unresolved conflicts remain UNVERIFIED.
66: Never import the target, an unproved project lemma, or a circular dependency
67: as E. Previously proved project modules require an expanded graph or a
68: versioned proof handoff. Do not attribute a combination of sources and a
69: project bridge to a single published theorem. A conjecture-dependent theorem
70: must retain that condition, which must be supplied legitimately at application.
71: 
72: ## 6. Every actual application
73: 
74: Give each actual E application an inference-local A ID. The same E applied
75: twice with different bindings has two A records, even within the same R.
76: For each A inspect the parameter/object bindings, prove every source
77: hypothesis from declared inputs or displayed local derivations, check types,
78: definitions and parameter ranges, identify substantive bridge N nodes, and
79: verify the resulting conclusion supports R's output. Record the evidence for
80: each individual hypothesis. “The theorem applies” is not a mapping.
81: Do not add an unproved hypothesis to close an application. An E passed at its
82: source does not automatically pass at any application site.
83: 
84: ## 7. Ownership of derived work
85: 
86: Put substantive specialization, scaling, change of normalization/domain/space/
87: norm/representation, combinations of sources, and prerequisite lemmas in N.
88: Each N lists its actual E/M/H/earlier-N inputs and its argument. Do not enlarge
89: the quoted theorem. Explicit elementary calculations and logical instantiation
90: may remain inside R; justify them rather than imposing needless graph nodes.
91: 
92: ## 8. Separate decisions and reproducible evidence
93: 
94: For each E write five separate review records: `literature_identity`,
95: `result_location`, `statement_fidelity`, `context_completeness`, and
96: `version_and_eligibility`. Each contains verdict, concrete notes and hashed
97: evidence. The first three must never be merged into one blanket PASS.
98: For each R/A write separate binding, per-hypothesis and conclusion reviews,
99: the source ID and the proved bridge IDs. Record actual reviewer, carrier,
100: shared context and reference material read. Self-audit is not independent.
101: 
102: Use PASS only after the check was performed with adequate evidence; FAIL for
103: an established mismatch/omission/invalid application; UNVERIFIED when necessary
104: evidence is missing. Inaccessible text does not establish nonexistence. An
105: established absence of the claimed result in the cited source is a FAIL.
106: Retain failed records and the exact reason, source location and affected nodes.
107: 
108: ## 9. Acceptance, invalidation and trust boundary
109: 
110: Every retained E check and every application must PASS before the graph can
111: receive DRAFT-AUDIT-PASSED. A load-bearing FAIL blocks acceptance. Source-verification UNVERIFIED can
112: support only the explicitly qualified continuation above; other unresolved
113: mathematical checks still block it. Ordinary whole-proof acceptance requires
114: every retained check to pass. Never replace a
115: missing verification with a historical audit or a Lean build. Changes to the
116: source/version, statement, definitions, bindings or condition proofs invalidate
117: affected reviews; bind the replacement whole receipt to new canonical hashes.
118: 
119: An inaccessible source suspends its citation verification, not the rest of
120: the workflow: continue available checks and explicitly conditional reasoning,
121: then report the unfinished citation checks and the UNVERIFIED overall audit
122: outcome. Descendants can be proved only relative to the explicit E assumption; the
123: whole result cannot receive an unconditional pass based on that source, and source inaccessibility alone is not a finding of mathematical error.
124: 
125: List all external dependencies in the final verdict. This audit is relative
126: to those identified theorems; it does not independently reprove their published
127: proofs or establish a Lean proof of E. Mechanical checks establish record
128: coverage and byte consistency, not authenticity or mathematical correctness.

value.full_target:
Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
value.conclusion: dim_H(F)=D+1, where F=E×[0,1] has the Euclidean product metric and D=dim_H(E); equivalently dim_H(E×[0,1])=dim_H(E)+1 in ℝ^{n+1}.

parameters.type: natural number (the nonnegative integer ambient dimension)
subset of the Euclidean space ℝ^n

hypotheses.origin: problem.md:21; the nonnegative integer is represented by a natural number, and its explicit range condition is retained.
problem.md:16-23; the disclosed user-approved nonemptiness assumption.

hypotheses.statement: E is compact in the Euclidean topology of ℝ^n.

definitions.type: family of Euclidean metric spaces indexed by natural numbers, together with their coordinate notation
definitions.definition: For each natural k, V(k)=ℝ^k, the functions from {0,...,k-1} to ℝ, with distance d(x,y)=(Σ_{j=0}^{k-1}(x_j-y_j)^2)^(1/2) and its metric topology and Borel measurable structure. V(0) consists of the single empty tuple. ℝ has its usual absolute-value distance. V(k)×ℝ always means the metric with squared distance d(x,y)^2+|t-u|^2, not the max-product metric. Concatenation (x,t)↦(x_0,...,x_{k-1},t) specifies the identification with V(k+1).

definitions.type: extended nonnegative diameter of a subset of a metric or extended metric space
definitions.definition: For an extended metric space X and A⊆X, diam(A)=sup{edist(x,y):x∈A,y∈A} in [0,∞], with supremum of the empty set equal to 0. On a metric space edist is ordinary distance viewed in [0,∞]. This is the native Metric.ediam. When diam(A) is bounded by a finite scale we identify it with its finite nonnegative real value. In particular empty sets and singletons have diameter zero.

definitions.type: positive-exponent unnormalized Hausdorff contents and measure, valued in [0,∞]
definitions.definition:
For a Euclidean set \(A\), exponent \(s>0\), and scale \(\delta>0\), put

\[
H^s_\delta(A)=\inf\left\{\sum_i(\operatorname{diam}U_i)^s:
 A\subseteq\bigcup_iU_i,\quad\operatorname{diam}U_i\leq\delta\right\},
\qquad H^s(A)=\sup_{\delta>0}H^s_\delta(A).
\]

Covers are countable, with empty members contributing zero.

binders.type: countable family of subsets of that Euclidean space

definitions.type: native Hausdorff measures on Borel extended metric spaces, indexed by real exponents
definitions.definition: μH[d] on a Borel extended metric space X denotes MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure d, defined natively as Measure.mkMetric(r↦r^d), the metric outer-measure construction with diameter gauge r^d followed by its Borel measure. The metric outer construction is the supremum over positive extended scales r of the infimum of Σ_i (sup_{h:U_i≠∅} diam(U_i)^d) over sequences U:ℕ→Set X covering the set and satisfying diam(U_i)≤r. Empty summands are zero, including at exponent zero. Native ENNReal real powers are used. The value formula for the resulting measure on arbitrary subsets is established by the registered native theorem; its identification with H for positive exponents is proved below.

binders.type: extended metric space with its Borel measurable structure

definitions.type: Hausdorff dimension of a subset of a metric space, valued in [0,∞]
definitions.definition: For a subset A of a metric space with its Borel structure, dim_H(A)=sup{u:u∈[0,∞) is finite and μH[u](A)=∞}, with supremum of the empty set zero. The metric space may be borelized when no measurable structure was specified. This is the native dimH definition. Thus dim_H(∅)=0 by this convention. In this task it is applied to Euclidean subsets and the Euclidean product metric of V(n)×ℝ.

definitions.type: subset of V(n)×ℝ with the Euclidean product metric
definitions.definition: F=E×I={(x,t):x∈E,t∈I}, using the squared-distance product metric specified in V. Its Euclidean identification is the concatenation map to V(n+1).
D=dim_H(E). When finiteness is proved, finite dimensions are also viewed as nonnegative real numbers through the canonical inclusion ℝ≥0→[0,∞].

definitions.type: predicate on subsets of metric spaces
definitions.definition: Compact(A) means that every family of open sets whose union contains A has a finite subfamily whose union contains A. The word compact has this finite-open-subcover meaning throughout.

definitions.type: Lebesgue measure on the Borel real line, also evaluated as outer measure on arbitrary sets
definitions.definition: λ is the native MeasureTheory.volume on ℝ, equivalently the Lebesgue measure whose outer measure is the infimum of sums of lengths of countable open-interval covers. As for any measure, λ is monotone, has λ(∅)=0, and is countably additive on disjoint measurable sets. These measure axioms are part of the measure structure, not any assertion of measurability of the arbitrary covering sets in this proof.

definitions.type: nonnegative Lebesgue integral for an arbitrary measure on a measurable space
definitions.definition: For a measurable space X, a measure ν on it, and f:X→[0,∞], LInt(ν,f)=∫⁻ f dν is the supremum of the simple-function integrals Σ_a a ν(g^{-1}{a}) over nonnegative measurable finite-range simple functions g≤f, with 0·∞=0. This is the native MeasureTheory.lintegral. For measurable f the value may be ∞; no finite-integrability premise is implicit.

targets.label: Hausdorff dimension of a product with an interval
targets.statement:
Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.

locals.type: Euclidean space with its Borel measurable structure
locals.declaration: Let X be any Euclidean space, including dimension zero, with its Borel measurable structure.
Fix an arbitrary real s; positivity is assumed only in the corresponding local implications.
For the monotonicity assertion fix B⊆X and assume A⊆B locally.
For the isometry assertion let Y be another Euclidean space.
Let φ:A→Y be distance preserving under L3.

argument.text: Fix a Euclidean space X, A⊆X and a real s; assume L1: s>0. Give X its Borel measurable structure. M001 with d=s identifies native μH[s](A) with the scale-cover formula. For positive s the empty-member summands vanish and each nonempty finite-diameter member has the ordinary real diameter power used in H. The supremum over extended positive scales equals the supremum over finite positive scales: the infimum at scale ∞ is no larger than the infimum at any finite scale. Countable covers are equivalent to sequences by enumeration and empty padding, with the same cost. Thus μH[s](A)=H^s(A). Restricting covers to smaller diameter bounds can only increase their infimum, so H^s_δ(A)≥H^s_r(A) whenever 0<δ≤r. The definition of H is its supremum over these contents; if that supremum is ∞, for every finite bound there is a scale exceeding the bound, and every smaller scale still exceeds it. Discharge L1 and universally generalize the arbitrary space, subset and exponent; F001 records this general statement with fresh bound names.

produces.statement: For every Euclidean space X0, subset A0⊆X0 and real p0>0, μH[p0](A0)=H^{p0}(A0); for every 0<d0≤r0, H^{p0}_{d0}(A0)≥H^{p0}_{r0}(A0). Also H^{p0}(A0)=sup_{d0>0}H^{p0}_{d0}(A0), and H^{p0}(A0)=∞ implies these contents are unbounded as the positive scale tends to zero.

argument.text: For the arbitrary X,A,s assume L6: s>0. Under the additional antecedent L7: s<dim_H(A), apply M002 with the nonnegative real u=s; F001 converts its conclusion to H^s(A)=∞, and discharging L7 proves that implication. Under L8: dim_H(A)<s, M003 similarly gives H^s(A)=0; discharge L8. Under L9: H^s(A)=0, F001 gives μH[s](A)=0≠∞, so M004 gives dim_H(A)≤s; discharge L9. Under L10: H^s(A)=∞, F001 and M005 give s≤dim_H(A); discharge L10. Discharge L6 and universally quantify the arbitrary space, subset and exponent. Nonnegativity of dimension follows from its definition as a supremum in [0,∞].

produces.statement: For every Euclidean space X0, A0⊆X0 and real p0>0: p0>dim_H(A0)⇒H^{p0}(A0)=0; p0<dim_H(A0)⇒H^{p0}(A0)=∞; H^{p0}(A0)=0⇒dim_H(A0)≤p0; H^{p0}(A0)=∞⇒dim_H(A0)≥p0. Also dim_H(A0)≥0 for every A0.

argument.text: For monotonicity fix B⊆X and temporarily assume L2: A⊆B. At every positive exponent s, any scale cover of B covers A, so its infimum bounds the content of A; taking suprema gives H^s(A)≤H^s(B). If dim_H(A)>dim_H(B), real order density supplies a finite positive exponent strictly between them (also when dim_H(A)=∞). F002 at that exponent and each set would give infinity on A and zero on B, contradicting the measure inequality. Hence dim_H(A)≤dim_H(B); discharge L2. For isometry let Y be Euclidean and assume L3: φ:A→Y preserves distances. Intersect the members of any cover of A with A and apply φ; they cover φ(A) with no greater diameters. Conversely inverse images in A of a cover of φ(A) cover A with no greater diameters, because φ preserves distance. Infima at each scale in both directions give equal contents at every positive exponent, and then H^s(φ(A))=H^s(A). If the dimensions differed, a positive finite exponent between them and F002 would again give zero on one side and infinity on the other. Discharge L3 and universally quantify X,A,B,Y,φ. The scale and critical assertions already hold universally by F001 and F002.

For arbitrary a>0, M012 at x=0 and q=a gives continuity of h↦h^a at zero, since 0≤a; its value is 0, so h^a→0 also through positive h. For arbitrary b<0, M013 gives h^b→∞ as h↓0. Finally the finite geometric identities Σ_{i=0}^{m-1}2^{-i-1}=1-2^{-m} and Σ_{i=0}^{m-1}2^{-i-2}=(1-2^{-m})/2 follow by telescoping the finite geometric sums. For m=0, 2^m≥m+1; the induction step follows from 2·(m+1)≥m+2 for m≥0. Thus 2^m≥m+1 for all natural m, so the remainders tend to zero by the Archimedean property, and taking suprema of the partial sums gives the two exported series values. Close the positive/negative exponent conditions as implications and quantify a,b.

argument.text: H003 and the open-cover definition of compactness give boundedness: the nested open balls about the origin with positive integer radii cover V(n), hence E; a finite subcover is contained in one such ball and therefore in [-R,R]^n for some real R≥1. For arbitrary s>0 and δ>0 (L1), the open balls of radius δ/2 centered at points of E cover E. H003 gives a finite subcover. Each ball has diameter at most δ by the triangle inequality, so its s-cost is finite, and the finite sum bounds H^s_δ(E). Discharge L1 and quantify s,δ.

argument.text: Choose R from F001. If n>0 (L2), for 0<h≤1 and a>n (L3), divide each coordinate interval [-R,R] into ceil(2R/h) closed equal subintervals, each of length at most h. The resulting cubes cover E, number at most (2R+1)^n h^{-n}, and have diameters at most √n h: the sum of the n squared coordinate differences is at most n h². Thus their total a-cost is at most (2R+1)^n n^{a/2} h^{a-n}. By the positive-power limit in N001 this tends to zero as h↓0. For every fixed target scale and positive cost tolerance, take h small enough for both inequalities; H^a at each scale and then H^a(E) are zero. N001 gives D≤a for every a>n, hence D≤n by order density. Discharge L3,L2. If n=0 (L4), H002 and the empty-tuple definition of V(0) give E=V(0), a singleton. Its singleton cover has zero s-cost at every scale for every s>0; N001 gives D≤s for all s>0, hence D=0. Discharge L4. In both cases D≥0 by N001 and D≤n. Together with F002 this proves the dimension, boundedness and finite-content assertions.

Finally the concatenation map in V has inverse that deletes the last coordinate and records it separately. For arbitrary x,y∈V(n) and real t,u, the squared distance between the two concatenated tuples is Σ_{j<n}(x_j-y_j)^2+(t-u)^2, exactly the squared product distance. Taking nonnegative square roots proves isometry, and the displayed inverse proves bijectivity. Its restriction sends F exactly to the required E×[0,1] in V(n+1), with no change of norm.

1: # Package local reasoning as true theorem nodes
2: 
3: The main graph has only E/M/H source propositions. A temporary assumption is
4: an argument-local device, never a trusted graph vertex. Every exported N/P is
5: a complete claim under the frozen original context. The audit inspects the
6: local derivation; surface implication syntax alone is insufficient.
7: The complete [neutral JSON example](../templates/quantified-implication-example.md)
8: shows an arbitrary binder, a local antecedent, its discharge and the full
9: quantified output. Follow this accounting rather than silently granting a
10: property in a local object's type.
11: 
12: ## Implication and contradiction
13: 
14: To prove `X -> Y`, introduce X inside one argument, derive Y from the declared
15: inputs, then discharge X into the antecedent. Output `X -> Y`, not Y. To use Y
16: unconditionally later, supply an actually proved X and apply implication
17: elimination. A local X and a proved X are not the same proof object.
18: 
19: To prove `not X`, derive false under local X and discharge X by negation
20: introduction. To prove P by classical contradiction, first produce the complete
21: theorem `not P -> false` (equivalently `not not P`), then apply the fixed
22: classical rule. A single R may combine the operations if every local assumption
23: is accounted for. No classical double-negation elimination under an
24: intuitionistic-only policy.
25: 
26: Example graph: N1 `(not P -> Q)`, N2 `not Q`, R1 outputs N3
27: `(not P -> false)`, R2 outputs P. The argument of R1 locally assumes not P,
28: applies N1 and N2, and closes that assumption. No `not P` root is added.
29: The fallacy “assume P, obtain P, discharge and output P” fails: its valid output
30: would be `P -> P`.
31: 
32: ## Cases
33: 
34: From an already proved `A or B or C`, obtain a common target Q by complete
35: conditional lemmas `A -> Q`, `B -> Q`, `C -> Q`, then disjunction elimination.
36: Alternatively prove `not A`, `not B` and conclude C using the original
37: disjunction. Eliminating A/B without a proved exhaustive disjunction cannot
38: establish C. A branch producing false can produce the common target by false
39: elimination; it does not make false an unconditional source proposition.
40: 
41: Proof bodies may contain all branches locally instead of exporting every
42: branch lemma. Check coverage, identical target/ambient context, and the absence
43: of sibling-branch fact/witness leakage. Introduce/discharge each branch-local
44: assumption in its actual scope.
45: 
46: ## Quantifiers, witnesses, and induction
47: 
48: For universal introduction use an arbitrary variable, then close its binder.
49: It must not occur free in an undischarged extra assumption. If the intended
50: theorem has a premise H(x), retain it in the quantified implication.
51: 
52: For existential elimination start from a proved existence statement, choose a
53: fresh local witness with exactly its stated properties, and prove a conclusion
54: independent of that witness's private identity. A witness depending on n does
55: not yield one witness valid for every n. Do not turn a local witness into a
56: globally available constant without a legitimate, recorded construction.
57: 
58: For natural-number induction prove the base and the complete step
59: `forall n, Q(n) -> Q(n+1)` and use induction to conclude `forall n, Q(n)`.
60: The induction hypothesis is local to the step; there is no circular graph edge.
61: If the step invokes the hypothesis at a transformed point s, include
62: `forall s` in the induction invariant. Well-founded induction needs the exact
63: well-founded relation/decrease justification; the word “induct” is not enough.
64: 
65: ## Local notation
66: 
67: Global symbols are reserved. Local binders can repeat across separate nodes
68: or separate binding scopes in a node, but cannot shadow a global symbol.
69: `sum_{k=1}^N` binds k only in that expression. Source theorem dummy variables
70: are alpha-renamed locally, not registered as a new global object each time.
71: Freshness, witness dependencies, constant uniformity, and binder scope are
72: mathematical audit obligations; a list of names does not verify the formula.
73: In v2, local declarations identify introduction kind/basis and inclusive S
74: start/end positions. An input-bound name needs instantiation; a witness needs
75: an actual existence premise. Local F facts record their complete statement,
76: statement-local binders, used objects and remaining assumptions. Neither a
77: fact nor a chosen witness may escape its scope. The checker accounts for
78: declared scopes; Audit A must also inspect the actual quantifier reasoning.
